the HoxA gene clusters have been evolving in a mosaic way in vertebrates and that the mosaic patterns have been different in different lineages.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the evolution of the HoxA locus was more dynamic in the actinopterygii than in the sarcopterygii, and this trend was accentuated by duplication of the Hox clusters in teleosts.
HoxA cluster evolution in ray-finned fishes has been more complex than previously thought.
the HoxA gene cluster in teleosts has undergone extensive sequence change since its duplication, with a peak of change in the earliest teleosts.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the HoxA duplication that occurred in the stem actineopterygians did not initiate the dynamic genomic evolution of the HoxA gene cluster that is observed in teleosts.
the HoxA gene repertoire and noncoding sequences have evolved independently in the bichir and the teleosts.
the HoxA genomic architecture of the earliest ray-finned fishes is more complex than that of the human HoxA cluster, and more dynamic than that of the shark HoxA cluster.
